# Use the specified ARM64 base image with OpenMPI, Flux, and EFA support for AWS
FROM ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-openmpi:ubuntu2204-efa-arm

# Set the working directory for the application
WORKDIR /app

# Install build dependencies, git for cloning, and certificates.
# Clean up apt cache to keep the image size down.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    cmake \
    git \
    ca-certificates && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Clone the latest branch of the LAMMPS source code, configure the build for MPI with the REAXFF package,
# compile, copy the executable to the system PATH, copy example files, and clean up the source directory.
RUN git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/lammps/lammps.git /lammps && \
    cd /lammps && \
    mkdir build && \
    cd build && \
    cmake -D PKG_REAXFF=on \
          -D BUILD_MPI=yes \
          -D CMAKE_C_COMPILER=mpicc \
          -D CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=mpicxx \
          ../cmake && \
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    cp lmp /usr/local/bin/ && \
    cp /lammps/examples/reaxff/HNS/* /app/ && \
    cd / && \
    rm -rf /lammps

# Verify that the LAMMPS executable is in the PATH
RUN which lmp

# Set the default command to launch a bash shell
CMD ["/bin/bash"]

#
# MiniCluster manifest to run a LAMMPS ReaxFF experiment on AWS ARM CPU instances.
# This configuration is designed for a multi-node setup, leveraging the Flux Operator
# to manage the distributed HPC workload.
#
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # The name of our MiniCluster instance.
  name: lammps-reax-aws-arm
  # Deploying to the default namespace as requested.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The number of pods (and nodes, assuming one pod per node) for the MiniCluster.
  # Set to 4 to satisfy the "run on up to 4 nodes" requirement.
  size: 4

  # Defines the application container to be run under Flux.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax
      # The command to execute. The Flux Operator will automatically prepend 'flux run'
      # to distribute this command across the tasks.
      command: lmp -v x 2 -v y 2 -v z 2 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite
      
      # The launcher pod is responsible for submitting the job. As we are submitting
      # directly with the CRD, this is not needed and must be false.
      launcher: false
      
      # Ensure the latest version of the container is always pulled.
      imagePullPolicy: Always
      
      # Resource requests and limits for AWS EFA networking devices.
      # This is required for high-performance networking on supported AWS instances.
      resources:
        limits:
          vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: 1
        requests:
          vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: 1

  # Specifies that the job resources should not be deleted after completion
  # to allow for inspection and debugging.
  cleanup: false
  
  # Logging settings for the Flux Operator.
  logging:
    # Enforces strict checking and error handling in logs.
    strict: true
    
  # Flux-specific configuration.
  flux:
    # This is an ARM instance, so we must specify the ARM architecture
    # and use a compatible Flux view image.
    arch: "arm"
    container:
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-ubuntu:arm-jammy
      # Disables the Flux sidecar container, running Flux directly in the main pod.
      # This is often used for performance or specific networking configurations.
      disable: true

updates.reason: The previous FOM of 12.507 katom-step/s on 4 nodes (256 cores) suggests the problem size (2x2x2 replication) was too small, leading to poor scaling efficiency. This attempt significantly increases the problem size by 8x (to 4x4x4 replication) to better utilize the available compute resources and improve the computation-to-communication ratio, which is expected to increase the FOM.

The FOM increased from 12.507 to 14.266 katom-step/s when the problem size was scaled from 2x2x2 to 4x4x4. This indicates that the application benefits from a larger problem size on this 4-node configuration. This attempt will further increase the problem size to 6x6x6 to test if this trend continues and push the FOM higher by improving the computation-to-communication ratio.

The previous attempt with a 6x6x6 problem size timed out, indicating it was too large for the allocated time/memory. The best performance so far was with the 4x4x4 size. This attempt will test an intermediate problem size of 5x5x5 to find the optimal point between the last successful run and the one that timed out.

Performance peaked at 14.657 katom-step/s with a 5x5x5 problem size. Increasing the problem size further to 6x6x6 resulted in a timeout, indicating the optimal point has been found and surpassed. The 5x5x5 configuration represents the best performance achieved within the operational limits of the system.

apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: lammps-reax-aws-arm
  namespace: default
spec:
  cleanup: false
  containers:
  - command: lmp -v x 5 -v y 5 -v z 5 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite
    image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax
    imagePullPolicy: Always
    launcher: false
    resources:
      limits:
        vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: '1'
      requests:
        vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: '1'
  flux:
    arch: arm
    container:
      disable: true
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-ubuntu:arm-jammy
  logging:
    strict: true
  pod:
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: m7g.16xlarge
  size: 4

manager.name: Build and Deploy LAMMPS
manager.description: Build a Docker container and deploy it as a Kubernetes Job.

context.environment: AWS CPU instance in Kubernetes to run across nodes
context.details:
You MUST use ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-openmpi:ubuntu2204-efa-arm as a base image. It includes OpenMPI and libfabric provided from the efa installer for AWS and the entire Flux Framework stack.
You MUST compile lammps setting the cxx compiler to mpicxx and the c compiler to mpicc.
Ensure all globbed files from examples/reaxff/HNS from the root of the lammps codebase are in the WORKDIR. Clone the latest branch of LAMMPS. You MUST put lmp on the PATH and run which lmp to ensure success.
You MUST build LAMMPS for a multi-node MPI environment

context.optimize:
You MUST maximize the LAMMPS FOM, *atom steps per second.  It could be Matom or katom.
You MUST parse a result to include the units for katom or Matom.
You MUST choose the largest problem size to maximize FOM. You MAY go up to 4 nodes. 
You MUST make an effort to increase problem size as much as you can.
context.resources: The resource spec you got earlier is for an autoscaling cluster, so the nodes possible are not there. You must add the nodeSelector to use node.kubernetes.io/instance-type m7g.16xlarge with 64 CPU, 256 GiB Memory, ARM (Graviton3). You are limited to up to 4 nodes.
context.testing: Run in.reaxff.hns in the pwd with lmp -v x 2 -v y 2 -v z 2 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite for testing only on all processes of one node.
context.details:
You MUST run on up to 4 nodes and you MUST set flux.container.disable to true.
You MUST set the containers imagePullPolicy to Always.
The Flux Operator uses flux run in the pwd with the tasks determined by the spec.tasks.
You MUST set resource requests and limits to use vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: 1
Since this is an ARM instance you MUST change the flux.container.image to be
ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-ubuntu:arm-jammy and set flux.arch: "arm".
